steps.what: Capture actual attendance, assessed progress and required student record changes
inputs: actual class attendance and assessed work

steps.what: Reconcile student identities and existing record entries against the captured actuals
Check required student record fields, dates and access restrictions
inputs: administrator-maintained required fields and access rules
outputs: complete corrected record version and remaining exceptions

steps.what: Review and approve the complete final student record version
inputs: complete corrected record version and remaining exceptions

steps.what: Save the approved student record in the same system

tasks.design: Configure {LMS} identity matching, required-field checks and access rules around instructor-captured actuals. The instructor resolves discrepancies and approves the final record before its separate save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual attendance and progress cannot be inferred from the planned class roster.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record constraints can highlight omissions and conflicting fields.
tasks.still_hard: Determine whether a discrepancy reflects a real student change or a recording error.
tasks.human_edge: Verify actual learning progress and sensitive changes.

ambition.what: Improve completeness within the existing record obligation.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3; confirm student-data permissions and consultation needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: student record systems can validate required fields and flag conflicting structured records.

assumptions: The instructor captures actual attendance, assessed progress, dates and authorised changes in s1; no new upstream capture is free. Administrators already own student IDs, required-field rules and permissions; unknown identities and policy exceptions remain manual.

Native LMS features come first. The central scenario applies only if manual matching and completeness checking remain today: s2 retains 60% and s3 50%. If native checks already cover this work, saving is zero.
Same-system save is approximately zero time today; the schema's one-point s5 carries no saving. There is no report or external send in this task boundary.

The complete final version exists at s3 before approval; any edit invalidates approval. Provisional B=100, R=80, gross=20; incremental focal upkeep=1; net=19. Shares are not measured baselines or derived from means priors.
unknowns: Existing validation coverage and actual discrepancy frequency.
research_questions: Observe record maintenance and time actual exception resolution separately from native validation.

already_counted.description: Final record review remains in s4

incremental.description: Review validation-rule exceptions and correct configuration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero where native checks already cover the work; high allows four additional hours of unresolved identity or completeness exceptions beyond the central net of 19.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Retrieve the approved lesson and demonstration materials for the class
inputs: current class roster and taught topic

steps.what: Teach basic English, life skills or workforce entry principles to the class
Demonstrate techniques and methods with examples and live student checks
Coach workshop practice, answer questions and adapt explanations to actual learner needs
Record and confirm actual class observations and follow-up needs
Save the confirmed observation note in the existing class record

tasks.design: Use existing {LMS} material access and class notes while the instructor teaches at {OTHER}, the classroom or workshop. Keep live explanation, demonstration, practice and response checking with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching requires observing understanding and responding during practice.
tasks.enabler_now: Native lesson access and note fields support delivery but establish no new time reduction.
tasks.still_hard: Adapt instruction when students misunderstand or lack confidence.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room and make practice safe and useful.

ambition.what: Retain live instruction without claiming shorter teaching time.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: instructors conduct demonstrations and respond to learners while learning systems provide material access and notes.

assumptions: Boundary is conducting the class, including material retrieval and immediate observation notes. Separate curriculum or test authoring is not silently included. Actual note capture is explicitly counted in s5, followed by a separate save; no report or message is required by this statement.

Native lesson indexing and structured notes are considered. No evidence establishes repeated hunting, transcription or duplicate entry, so no saving is assigned to s1 or s5. Same-system s6 is approximately zero time and earns no saving.

OTHER is the physical classroom or workshop. Students provide actual answers and practice; the instructor observes them rather than inferring understanding from attendance. No machine messages or teaching replacement are proposed.
Provisional B=100, R=100, gross=0; incremental=0; net=0. Shares are scenario allocations independent of means priors.
unknowns: Whether material retrieval or immediate notes contain demonstrable avoidable work.
research_questions: Observe a class and separate retrieval, live teaching and note work before considering any change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported reduction after separating material access, actual note capture and same-system save from live teaching.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish classroom rules and maintain order

steps.what: Review current behavior policies and actual class needs before establishing rules
inputs: actual class needs observed by instructor
outputs: confirmed policy constraints and class requirements

steps.what: Draft understandable behavior rules and classroom procedures within confirmed constraints
inputs: confirmed policy constraints and class requirements
outputs: complete draft rules and intended class audience

loop.input: confirmed policy constraints, class requirements and intended audience
loop.output: proposed rules with source references and unresolved questions
loop.check: Instructor checks meaning, omissions, fairness and consistency with policy; the model cannot add sanctions
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual wording
loop.why_not_simpler: Plain-language wording for differing learner needs needs semantic interpretation; templates remain the first option

steps.what: Review and approve the final rules and publication audience
inputs: complete draft rules and intended class audience

steps.what: Publish the approved rules to the specified class audience
Explain rules and procedures and check students understand them
Enforce behavior rules and restore order in response to actual classroom incidents
Record and confirm actual incidents, actions and follow-up decisions
Save the confirmed restricted incident note

tasks.design: Use approved {DOCS} policy and class requirements to assist rule wording, then publish the instructor-approved version through {LMS}. Keep explanation, enforcement and actual incident capture with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Generic rules may be difficult for adult learners to understand or may omit local constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting step can propose clearer wording while native class publication handles delivery.
tasks.still_hard: Apply rules fairly in a live classroom.
tasks.human_edge: Understand context and respond proportionately to behavior.

ambition.what: Make existing rules understandable without expanding automated enforcement.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-4; review learner-data access and consultation needs

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: language models can draft plain-language rules and learning systems can publish approved class material.

assumptions: s1 counts reading actual policy and identifying class needs; administrator supplies existing policy, instructor supplies actual needs. No student incident data enters the drafting model. Missing or conflicting constraints require manual drafting.

Native policy templates come first. Central applies only when new class-specific wording and a real separate publication action occur today; s2 retains 60%, s4 removes only publication handling. Routine saves already in the same system provide no saving.

OTHER is the classroom. Explanation, enforcement and actual note capture remain unchanged. s7 confirms the finished note before s8 saves; s3 follows the finished rules before s4 publishes. Edits invalidate approvals.
Provisional B=100, R=89, gross=11; incremental focal upkeep=1; net=10. Shares are illustrative, not observed baselines or means-prior allocations.
unknowns: Frequency of rule revision and whether native templates already suffice.
research_questions: Review actual rule revisions, publication effort and semantic corrections with instructors.

already_counted.description: Final rule and audience review in s3

incremental.description: Maintain approved rule sources and inspect drafting failures

approvals.approved_version: final rules and specified class audience

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero when templates and native publication already cover the work; high allows three extra hours of wording corrections beyond central net 10.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare tests and issue assessed grades

steps.what: Select test objectives, format and rubric from the taught content
inputs: existing course objectives and approved assessment rules

steps.what: Prepare written questions, oral prompts and performance tests with proposed answer guidance
outputs: complete proposed test, rubric, answer guidance and intended class

loop.purpose: Draft test material aligned to taught content
loop.input: confirmed specification, rubric and approved taught materials
loop.output: proposed questions, oral prompts, performance instructions and answer guidance
loop.check: Instructor checks correct answers, ambiguity, difficulty, accessibility and content alignment against source material; model cannot set grades
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then instructor writes remaining items
loop.why_not_simpler: An approved item bank comes first; genuinely new questions and distractors require semantic judgement beyond field substitution

steps.what: Review and approve the completed test, rubric and intended class
inputs: complete proposed test, rubric, answer guidance and intended class
outputs: approved final test and administration instructions

steps.what: Administer the approved written, oral and performance tests and capture actual responses
inputs: approved final test and administration instructions
outputs: captured student responses and observed performance evidence

steps.what: Assess actual responses and performance and enter provisional grades with reasons
inputs: captured student responses and observed performance evidence

steps.what: Review and approve final grades and each student's release destination
inputs: actual response evidence and student identity

steps.what: Issue the approved grades through the existing student grade release control
outputs: issued grades available to correct students

tasks.design: Use approved taught material in {DOCS} to draft assessment items for instructor review. The instructor administers tests at {OTHER}, the classroom, assesses actual responses in {LMS}, and separately approves and releases final grades.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing new assessment wording can take effort even when objectives and rubrics exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can propose source-aligned items without assigning grades.
tasks.still_hard: Determine whether an item fairly assesses the intended skill and whether a learner demonstrated it.
tasks.human_edge: Judge oral and practical performance in context.

ambition.what: Reduce supported item drafting while preserving instructor assessment.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5; verify assessment governance and approved source access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: language models can propose assessment wording while instructors check validity and retain grading authority.

assumptions: s1 counts selecting actual taught content, objectives, format and rubric. Existing course owners supply approved source materials; missing content is not invented. Student response capture and grade entry are fully counted in s4 and s5.

An existing item bank and native assessment controls come first. Central reduces only new item preparation by 40%; native objective scoring already automated earns no additional saving. Oral and performance grading remain manual.

s3 approves the finished test before administration; s6 approves final entered grades and destinations before release. Any edit invalidates approval. The one-point release control has no assumed saving, like a near-zero same-system save.

No hidden grade-report or email workflow is assumed. Provisional B=100, R=90, gross=10; incremental focal source/item maintenance=2; net=8. Shares are scenario allocations, not measured baselines or means priors.
unknowns: Item-bank coverage and correction time for proposed items.
research_questions: Compare preparation and review time for genuinely new items while checking validity and grade consistency.

already_counted.description: Final test review retained in s3

incremental.description: Maintain approved drafting sources and inspect item failures

approvals.approved_version: completed test, rubric and intended class
final grades and student release destinations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero when the existing item bank covers preparation; high allows three additional hours of item correction beyond central net 8.
